The rotor includes at least one second outlet extending from a portion of the separation space to the space for discharge of at least one higher density component separated from the fluid during operation. The second outlet is arranged for intermittent discharge by an intermittent discharge system and one of the seals is formed by the intermittent discharge system.

A centrifugal separator has a housing that defines an internal area kept sealed from the surrounding environment and maintained at a pressure lower than ambient pressure by at least one seal. A rotor is mounted to rotate about a rotational axis and contains a separation chamber inside it. During use, the fluid is subjected to centrifugal separation in this chamber, causing at least one denser component and at least one less dense component to separate from the fluid.

At least one inlet reaches into the rotor to supply the fluid to the separation chamber. At least one first outlet leads out from the rotor to remove at least one component that has been separated from the fluid during operation. The rotor also has at least one second outlet running from a part of the separation chamber to the surrounding internal area, for releasing at least one denser component separated from the fluid during operation. This second outlet is configured to discharge intermittently through an intermittent discharge system, and one of the seals is provided by that intermittent discharge system.
outputs.L3:
A centrifugal separator comprises a sealed casing configured to maintain an underpressure relative to the surrounding atmosphere. Within the casing, a rotor is arranged to rotate about a rotational axis. The rotor defines a separation space in which a supplied fluid mixture is separated into different components according to their respective densities during rotation.

At least one inlet is provided for introducing the fluid mixture into the separation space of the rotor. As the rotor rotates, centrifugal forces act on the fluid, causing denser components to move radially outward while less dense components remain closer to the rotational axis. At least one first outlet is arranged to discharge one of the separated components from the rotor during operation of the separator.

The separator further includes a second outlet configured to discharge, intermittently, a component having a higher density than the component discharged through the first outlet. This intermittent discharge may be used, for example, to remove accumulated heavy phase material or solids from the separation space. The system responsible for the intermittent discharge is also arranged to form one of the seals of the sealed casing, thereby contributing both to the controlled discharge of the higher density component and to the maintenance of the underpressure within the casing.
outputs.L4:
A centrifugal separator comprises a stationary casing enclosing a rotating rotor. The casing is sealed from the surrounding atmosphere and is arranged to be maintained at a pressure below atmospheric pressure during operation. Within the casing, the rotor is mounted for rotation about an axis of rotation and is configured to receive a fluid mixture containing at least two components of different densities. When the rotor is driven at high speed, centrifugal forces cause the fluid mixture to separate into a higher-density component and a lower-density component.

The rotor includes an inlet for supplying the fluid mixture to a separation chamber formed within the rotor. During rotation, the higher-density component is displaced radially outwardly, while the lower-density component remains closer to the rotational axis. The separated components are then removed from the rotor through separate discharge arrangements. A first outlet is provided for discharging one of the separated components, such as the lower-density component, from the rotor. A second outlet is provided for discharging the higher-density component.

The second outlet is arranged to discharge the higher-density component intermittently. Instead of continuously removing this component, the separator periodically opens the second outlet to allow accumulated higher-density material to be expelled from the rotor. This intermittent discharge may occur automatically during operation and may be controlled by a discharge mechanism associated with the rotor. The higher-density component discharged through the second outlet is released into a space inside the sealed casing, from which it can be collected or removed.

The intermittent discharge system is also configured to perform a sealing function. In particular, a part of the intermittent discharge arrangement forms one of the seals between the rotating rotor and the stationary casing, or between different pressure regions of the separator. As a result, the system used for intermittently discharging the higher-density component is integrated with the sealing arrangement of the separator.

This integration provides a compact and efficient construction. By allowing the intermittent discharge mechanism to also serve as a seal, the separator reduces the need for additional separate sealing components. This can simplify the design, reduce the number of parts, improve reliability, and help maintain the desired under-pressure condition within the casing. The arrangement therefore combines the functions of controlled discharge and pressure sealing in a single system, improving the overall operation and construction of the centrifugal separator.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps identify a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when someone says “the book,” they are usually referring to a particular book that both the speaker and listener know about.

Although “the” is a small word, it can change the meaning of a sentence. Compare “I saw a dog” with “I saw the dog.” The first sentence introduces any dog, while the second points to a specific dog. This makes “the” useful for clarity and precision.

The word also appears in many names and titles, such as “The United States,” “The Great Gatsby,” and “The Beatles.” In these cases, it becomes part of the identity of a place, book, or group.

In everyday speech and writing, “the” often goes unnoticed because it is so familiar. However, without it, English would feel less natural and less exact. This simple word helps organize meaning and guide understanding, proving that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a centrifugal separator with a sealed under-pressure casing, a rotating separation rotor, inlet and outlets, and an intermittent discharge system that also forms one of the seals.
counterfactuals.output: A centrifugal separator comprises a sealed casing maintained at an under-pressure relative to ambient pressure, a separation rotor arranged to rotate within the casing about an axis of rotation, an inlet for supplying a feed mixture to the rotor, and at least one outlet for discharging a separated phase from the rotor. The separator further comprises an intermittent discharge system configured to periodically discharge a separated component from the rotor through a discharge path. The intermittent discharge system includes a movable discharge member arranged between the rotor and the casing, the movable discharge member being operable between a closed position and an open discharge position. In the closed position, the movable discharge member forms a sealing arrangement between the rotating rotor and the sealed casing, thereby contributing to maintaining the under-pressure within the casing. In the open discharge position, the movable discharge member permits intermittent discharge of the separated component while limiting pressure loss from the casing. The arrangement enables separation under reduced-pressure conditions with controlled periodic removal of separated material and with reduced need for separate sealing components.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise technical description of an invention involving a centrifugal separator where a rotor separates high- and low-density components and intermittently discharges the heavier component into an evacuated casing space.
counterfactuals.output: A centrifugal separator includes a rotor mounted within a surrounding casing and defining a separation chamber for a feed mixture containing components of different densities. During rotation, the mixture is separated into a relatively high-density component collected radially outwardly in the rotor and a relatively low-density component collected radially inwardly. The rotor is provided with discharge openings controlled by an intermittent discharge mechanism for periodically releasing the high-density component from the separation chamber. The casing defines an evacuated space surrounding the rotor, so that each intermittent discharge expels the high-density component from the rotor into the evacuated casing space with reduced aerodynamic resistance and minimized pressure disturbance. The low-density component is continuously or separately withdrawn from the rotor through an outlet.

counterfactuals.output: A centrifugal separator apparatus comprises a stationary casing arranged to be maintained at an under-pressure and a rotor rotatable in the casing about an axis of rotation. The rotor defines a separation space and is provided with an inlet for a fluid mixture to be separated, a first outlet for a separated light phase, and a second outlet for separated heavier material. An intermittent discharge system associated with the second outlet is configured to open and close the second outlet during operation and, in its closed state, to form a seal preventing communication between the separation space and the surrounding under-pressure casing.
